relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with SSADH deficiency and a homozygous ALDH5A1 variant: "Genetic testing revealed a homozygous mutation in the aldehyde dehydrogenase 5 family member A1 (ALDH5A1) gene."
method_note: Hand-extracted from the full text (no tables). Three individuals: the index patient (rule 5 'patient'); her sibling who died at one year of severe convulsions (affected relative, untested: 'Genetic testing was ordered for her at that time but unfortunately was not done'; no variant row); and the Horino et al. [7] patient from the Discussion (individual-level facts: age nine months, status epilepticus, regression, myoclonus, brain atrophy). The sentence 'She died at our hospital of respiratory failure...' follows the sibling sentence and its genetic testing was not done, so it was read as about the sibling (hence sibling sex female); this pronoun reading is an interpretation. Consanguinity was not copied to the sibling. The first documented 1981 case [3,6] was not given a row (no individual-level fact beyond the diagnostic finding). The mother (healthy, untested) was not given a row. Variant: only a genomic position is printed ('G->A substitution at chr6:24505155', no genome build, no transcript, cDNA or protein HGVS); 'abnormal protein translation ... at amino acid position 223' is a prediction attributed to Akaboshi et al. [5], not an assay or classification, so functional evidence, pathogenicity and variant type are 'not reported'. Inheritance not reported (no parental testing). Normal MRI (normal cortex, white matter, cerebellum, ventricular system, myelination) recorded as excluded abnormalities of those named structures under D-27; the checklist items 'cerebral or cerebellar atrophy' and 'T2 hyperintensity...' were left 'not reported' because atrophy and nuclei signal are not named. Horino [7] patient: the age 'nine-month-old' fits neither onset nor last evaluation, so ages are 'not reported'; vital status alive from 'This patient survived'. Contradictions/oddities in the paper: the abstract and Discussion call it a 'fetal case'/'fetal presentation' although the patient is a four-month-old infant; the Discussion says 'especially in the absence of a familial history' although the Case presentation reports a sibling who died of severe convulsions; 'death at four months' age (P4M) is taken from the title.
